body:
The only issue I see about the extra effort to preserve the exit code is that we can get to this problem:
```
> bash -c 'exit 5'
> $Global:LASTEXITCODE
5
> gci inexistentfolder
Get-ChildItem: Cannot find path '/home/my-user/inexistentfolder' because it does not exist
> $Global:LASTEXITCODE
5
``` 
I would check it myself later, but it would be easier if you can point me to a place in the Rust code where the exit code is relevant for some process, then I would totally agree that it is necessary to find to preserve the exit code and a way to tell apart whether the last command was an internal Powershell (exit code is irrelevant) command or an external one (exit code is relevant), if the exit code is only used in the `starship` command to define the color/symbol of the prompt I would argue that a simple 0 or 1 is enough.
